known_public_status: The Erdos Problems page still marks the problem open. The discussion thread contains a comment claiming a Matomaki-Radziwill deduction and a later caveat that lower density does not establish existence of natural density. Treat as a partial/conditional-golden record unless a human expert accepts the formulation.
normalized_statement: For every epsilon, eta > 0, find k such that the set G_k(epsilon) = {n: P(prod_{j=0}^k (n+j)) > n^{1-epsilon}} has density at least 1-eta. The RLVR proof record proves lower asymptotic density at least 1-eta via upper density control of the exceptional set.
original_statement: Is it true that for every epsilon, eta > 0 there exists a k such that the density of n for which P(n(n+1)...(n+k)) > n^{1-epsilon} is at least 1-eta, where P(m) is the greatest prime divisor of m?
target: Prove upper density of the exceptional set B_H(epsilon) tends to 0 as H tends to infinity, then set k=H-1.
title: Erdos Problem #1201: largest prime divisor of products of consecutive integers
